base_member_text: [L161-L170] (LOW/error-path-output) nf90_inquire copies local inquiry outputs without checking success and overwrites the first status with nf_inq_format when formatNum is requested.
audit_member_text: [L161-L170] (MED/error-handling) nf90_inquire copies uninitialized local outputs after failed inquiries and overwrites the first inquiry status with the format-query status when formatNum is present.

adversarial.rationale: nf90_inquire has uninitialized automatic output locals and unconditional presence-based copies, then assigns the format-query status over the first status (netcdf_file.f90:156-172). No success guard or initializer exists in the enclosing module; although an invalid ncid normally makes both calls fail, that does not remove the unconditional undefined-output copies or the status overwrite.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L56-L62,L79-L85] (MED/intent-contract) The multiprocess create/open wrappers declare chunk-size hints INTENT(IN) although the corresponding ordinary wrappers treat these underlying library arguments as writable INOUT values.
audit_member_text: [L56-L62,L79-L85] (MED/intent-contract) The multiprocess create/open wrappers declare chunk-size hints INTENT(IN) while passing them directly to routines that return the selected chunk size, unlike the INOUT contract used by the ordinary wrappers.

adversarial.rationale: The mp wrappers pass their INTENT(IN) chunk hint itself, with no local copy, to the legacy routines (netcdf_file.f90:56-86). The bundled manual says those routines behave like nf__create/nf__open except for the base PE (netcdf_f90.3:925-938), while the ordinary wrappers explicitly use INOUT and return the selected hint; netcdf_visibility.f90:7 exposes the mp wrappers and no platform exclusion removes them.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

audit_member_text: [L56,L58,L79,L81] (LOW/keyword-contract) The public multiprocess wrappers expose inconsistent misspelled keyword names initalsz and chunksizeint, making keyword-based calls prone to incompatibility.
